items.title: Roche’s Genentech notches 2nd breast cancer approval for oral SERD in a week
items.snippet: The FDA approval of Wilserdly—the first new hormone therapy option for patients with early-stage breast cancer in more than 20 years—is the second straight greenlight for Roche’s drug, which got the nod for an advanced breast cancer subtype last week.

items.title: ProMIS’ new CCO is ready to write next chapter in Alzheimer’s after leaving Biogen
items.snippet: Ivana Rubino has joined neurodegenerative biotech ProMIS Neurosciences as chief commercial officer, with 15 years of experience in the brutal Alzheimer’s field as her guide.

items.title: BMS loses CFO to Coca-Cola on heels of R&D overhaul
items.snippet: The announcement comes less than two weeks after Bristol Myers Squibb merged its research and development departments under one leader.

items.title: Sanofi’s new CEO Garijo strikes 2026’s largest pharma deal with $41B for Insmed
items.snippet: Insmed will bolster Sanofi’s immunology and inflammation portfolio, which is currently led by Regeneron-partnered blockbuster Dupixent.

items.title: Biotech’s fear of global expansion is overblown, risks destroying asset value
items.snippet: The perceived threat of Most Favored Nation drug pricing is keeping many companies out of international markets. But for some medicines, the costs of delaying entry run high.

items.title: FDA approves BridgeBio’s Welgemda as 1st targeted therapy for rare muscle disease
items.snippet: Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas called the approval of BridgeBio’s limb-girdle muscular dystrophy therapy “a historic milestone” for patients and families living with the disease.

items.title: Erasca’s early data show profile that could challenge RevMed in pancreatic cancer: Analysts
items.snippet: In updated Phase 1 data, Erasca’s ERAS-0015 showed a robust response rate in pancreatic cancer subgroups where Revolution Medicines’ recently-approved Rasonque was weaker, leading Jefferies to write that the investigational molecular glue could have an advantage over the approved therapy.

items.title: Sharon Mates’ next act: Ritzey banks $112M to target Down syndrome and diabetes
items.snippet: After J&J’s $14.6 billion buyout of Intra-Cellular Therapies, the biotech’s former CEO Sharon Mates is still chasing intracellular signaling, this time with Ritzey Therapeutics for metabolic and neurologic diseases.

items.title: Invivyd plans FDA run for COVID-19 preventative, teeing up ‘new era for immunization’
items.snippet: Invivyd plans on ushering in a “new era for immunization” with its COVID-19 prevention antibody that is designed using the same antibody backbone as the biotech’s emergency-authorized Pemgarda.

items.title: Orca lays off employees, focuses on launch of newly approved cell therapy
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Lilly’s 15th M&A deal of 2026 brings LoQus23’s Huntington’s work in house for $725M
items.snippet: LoQus23 Therapeutics is a good match for Eli Lilly’s professed goal of finding biotechs that provide small, early, risky bets.

items.title: Capricor CEO says FDA never gave DMD cell therapy a ‘fair shake’
items.snippet: The FDA rejected Capricor Therapeutics’ Duchenne muscular dystrophy cell therapy for a second time on Friday, citing data integrity issues. CEO Linda Marbán told BioSpace she was shocked and explains why she thinks this reason is suspect.

items.title: With two upcoming FDA decisions, ‘oddball’ Praxis is on the cusp of commercialization
items.snippet: As the FDA homes in on a unified rare disease strategy, Praxis Precision Medicines is anticipating its first approval with two near-term shots on goal—a treatment for a devastating rare seizure condition, followed by a drug for a more common neuro condition.

items.title: At Jefferies 2026, investors put CGT manufacturing under the microscope
items.snippet: Investors are increasingly scrutinizing manufacturing strategies, scalability and cost of goods long before commercialization, as CMC setbacks and production challenges reshape funding decisions across cell and gene therapy.

items.title: Capricor’s regulatory odyssey for DMD cell therapy hits second FDA rejection
items.snippet: A new proposed indication was not enough to get deramiocel across the regulatory finish line. The FDA has again turned away the cell therapy, which is being developed for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, for the second time in as many years.

items.title: FDA will miss rare decision deadline for Savara candidate after three-month delay
items.snippet: Savara shares dropped 18% on the news, though analysts remain confident in approval, instead pointing to potential “bandwidth issues” at the FDA.

items.title: RevMed pads Rasonque’s first-line survival advantage in pancreatic cancer with early data
items.snippet: The new data could help boost Revolution Medicines beyond the currently estimated $14.5 billion in peak sales for the recently approved RAS(ON) inhibitor, Truist Securities predicts.

items.title: An Insmed takeout by Sanofi would be ‘clear strategic fit’ in respiratory space
items.snippet: If it came to fruition, the rumored deal between Sanofi and Insmed would likely be the year’s largest, with one analyst putting a potential value for the biotech as high as $40 billion.

items.title: Merck-Kelun ADC scores survival win in Phase 3 gastroesophageal cancer trial
items.snippet: Licensed from Kelun-Biotech, Merck’s TROP2-targeting antibody drug conjugate sac-TMT improved overall survival in advanced gastroesophageal cancer while missing on two secondary endpoints.

items.title: Novartis projects slowed growth, pins hopes on billions in pipeline potential
items.snippet: With Kisqali going off patent and decreasing prices impacting sales, Novartis has narrowed sales guidance to 5% growth. But management remains steadfast that they have a plan to get back on track.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
